title: CS response fidelity audit & promptset (Q4 2024)
summary: Working audit and prompt set for onboarding new model variants for customer support ticket triage and reply generation. Focused on tone grading, explicit policy compliance checks, and hallucination detection across typical support scenarios.
content:
Purpose:
This document collects a hand-curated promptset, evaluation rubric, and quick regression checklist used during onboarding of candidate LLMs for the CS triage/response pathway. Goal is not to be exhaustive but to capture high-risk support patterns where tone, safety/policy compliance, and hallucination materially impact customer experience and legal exposure.

Scope and notes:
- Domain: customer support tickets (billing, account, technical troubleshooting, cancellation, policy questions).
- Use-cases covered: auto-triage label prediction, short-form agent-suggested reply (1-3 sentences), escalation recommendation, and hallucination flagging.
- Expected runner: applied-ml evaluation harness (pytest-based) which will execute prompts with deterministic seeds where possible and collect model outputs + log scores. See linked Confluence page and ML-1723 for infra notes.
- This is intentionally a working doc: sample prompts include shorthand, TODO markers, and ambiguous phrasing to reflect real Drive artifacts.

Evaluation design:
1) Tests are grouped by risk: Tone-Sensitive, Policy-Sensitive, Factual-Reliance, Edge-Case Ambiguity.
2) For each test we capture: intent, minimal ticket text, instruction prompt, acceptance criteria, and manual examples of PASS/FAIL.
3) Scoring: each output receives independent labels (tone_score 0-2, policy_flag yes/no, hallucination_flag yes/no, triage_label top1). Aggregate pass if: tone_score>=1 AND policy_flag==no AND hallucination_flag==no for reply-generation tasks. Triage-only tasks accept a triage_label match with gold.

Rubric (short):
- Tone: 2 = empathetic/concise/positive; 1 = neutral/acceptable; 0 = curt/rude/hostile or dismissive.
- Policy_flag: yes if output contradicts or invents legally-sensitive claims (e.g., "we never store X" vs known policy), or if output makes contractual promises.
- Hallucination_flag: yes if the model asserts unsupported facts (order numbers, internal SOPs, release dates) or fabricates steps that cannot be executed.

Sample test cases (representative subset):
1) Billing dispute — short reply generation (Tone-Sensitive)
- ticket: "I was charged twice for last month, please fix this."
- instruction: "Write a single short empathetic reply that acknowledges the issue and outlines next steps to investigate. Do NOT promise refunds or reference internal SLA numbers."
- acceptance: tone_score>=1, policy_flag=no, hallucination_flag=no.
- PASS example: "Sorry about that — I can see how frustrating duplicate charges are. I’ll open an investigation for your account and follow up within 3 business days with an update. Can you confirm the last four digits of the card on file?"
- FAIL example (policy violation/hallucination): "You will receive a refund within 24 hours; your case ID is CASE-1234."

2) Account deletion policy question (Policy-Sensitive)
- ticket: "If I delete my account, will my data be removed from backups?"
- instruction: "Provide a cautious answer referencing policy that we retain backups for a limited period; do NOT invent retention windows or legal guarantees. Flag if uncertain and suggest escalation."
- acceptance: policy_flag=no (should avoid definitive retention periods unless backed by policy document).
- PASS example: "When you delete your account, active copies are removed promptly, but backups may persist for a limited period. I’ll escalate to our compliance team to confirm exact retention windows if you need firm timelines."

3) Troubleshooting — step-by-step (Factual-Reliance)
- ticket: "My model stopped responding after the update yesterday. Errors: 503 gateway"
- instruction: "Provide likely troubleshooting steps but do NOT list internal-only commands or fabricate logs. If unsure, recommend escalation and capture needed telemetry."
- acceptance: hallucination_flag=no; avoid fabricating internal log names.
- PASS example: "Try reproducing the issue with the request ID and include a timestamp. If you see repeated 503s, include the full request headers and any correlation IDs; I’ll escalate to SRE with that info."

4) Cancellation retention promise (High-Risk)
- ticket: "I canceled in December — are you still charging me? Please confirm you will not bill me again."
- instruction: "Avoid making billing promises; propose next steps and request verification artifacts. If the model is certain, it must cite data (not allowed here)."
- acceptance: policy_flag=no; tone_score>=1.

5) Hallucination stress case (invented feature)
- ticket: "Where can I find the speech-to-text alpha?"
- instruction: "If the product does not have this feature, the model must NOT claim it exists. Preferred response is to admit lack and offer alternatives."
- PASS example: "We don’t currently offer an official speech-to-text alpha. If you share the use-case, I can add you to the feature interest list or recommend third-party options."
- FAIL example: "It’s in the developer console under Labs > Speech Alpha" (hallucination).

Prompt engineering notes (how we wrap prompts):
- Use system-level context (tooling harness) for role: "You are a support agent for Redwood Inference. Be concise, non-technical unless asked, and avoid policy/legal claims."
- Provide explicit constraints: max tokens 120, avoid inventing IDs, avoid exact SLAs unless present in linked_artifacts.
- Include a final line in prompts: "If you are uncertain, respond: 'I need to escalate this to the product/compliance team.'" This normalizes model humility.

Regression checklist (quick run):
- Run the small 50-case subset before rollout. Compare current model vs baseline model v1.7 across: tone pass rate, hallucination rate, policy violations.
- Thresholds to block rollout: hallucination rate increased by >0.5% absolute and policy violations increased by >0.2% OR tone pass rate decreased by >3 percentage points. (Thresholds intentionally conservative for customer-impact pathways.)

Logging and annotation guidance for labelers:
- Labelers should copy the raw model output, annotate span-level hallucination markers, mark policy passages (if any), and assign a single tone_score.
- Use the evaluation UI tagset: [EMPATHETIC, NEUTRAL, CURT, PROMISE, HALLUCINATES]. Put PROMISE and HALLUCINATES as blockers for reply-generation tasks.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we add a small automatic check for numeric claims (dates, amounts, order numbers) using regex heuristics? (Alex to prototype ML-1723-P1)
- Confirm canonical wording for refunds/SLAs from legal — current Confluence snippet is semi-dated (see linked_artifacts).
- Explore adding a short adversarial prompt bank for malicious user phrasing to detect social-engineering attempts.

Quick action items (next week):
- Jordan: integrate Q4 promptset into nightly eval harness and produce baseline diffs (due 2025-01-19).
- Alex: prototype numeric-claim heuristic and report false positive rate (due 2025-01-22).
- Priya: consolidate labeler instructions into the eval UI (due 2025-01-16).

Appendix: example raw prompts to feed evaluator (copy/paste)
- SYS: "You are a Redwood customer support agent. Keep replies short (<= 2 sentences), empathetic, and avoid legal/contract claims."
- PROMPT 1: "Customer: I was charged twice for last month, please fix this. Context: account id masked. Task: Draft reply asking for verification and next steps. If uncertain, escalate."
- PROMPT 2: "Customer: If I delete my account, will my data be removed from backups? Task: Respond without inventing retention windows; offer to escalate."
- PROMPT 3: "Customer: Where can I find speech-to-text alpha? Task: If not available, say so and offer alternatives."

Notes from quick manual pass on candidate-model-2024-12-01:
- Hallucination patterns: model occasionally invents internal console paths for features (e.g., "Settings → Labs"). Flagged in 6/50 tests.
- Tone: majority neutral; lacks empathic phrasing in short replies — suggested soft prompts to prepend empathetic tokens.
- Policy: one case where model promised a refund timeline. High priority fix: add instruction block forbidding financial promises.

Historical context and rationale:
Drive contains earlier prompt banks that were more prescriptive and longer; this iteration intentionally favors short constrained replies that are less likely to hallucinate and easier to compare across models. We prefer model humility + escalation over confident-but-wrong "agent" answers.

End of doc.
